thread.title: Don’t throw out these Teflon stocks as you flee the market

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Don’t throw out these Teflon stocks as you flee the market
text:
The big day is finally here. So stand up to St. Valentine, shake your fist and say “no more roses, no more chocolates!”
Roses are red
Violets are blue
Buffett is patient
Unlike you #FinTwitValentines
— Edward Taussig (@edtaussig) February 14, 2018 Alas, it’s the OTHER big day that’s got most people zero-focused this am. Consumer prices and retail sales hit this morning, and stock futures aren’t liking a CPI surge for January one bit. Some have been warning that this data could send us back to the dark days of last week.
Whether or not Wall Street has blown this indicator all out of proportion , be warned that this inflation tension could turn into a thing. “This really is going to be the main focal point every month this year, we think,” says Jim Reid, strategist at Deutsche Bank, in a note this morning.
Add that to the recent market upheaval, and it seems there’s no better time for the long-term investor to steer the course, keep a stiff upper lip, etc. — right? That brings us to our call of the day , from Daily Reckoning’s Greg Guenthner , who says the smart money is keeping a steady eye on trends that are pointing to tech strength.
“Strong trends usually persist,” says Guenthner, who adds that rather than predict the next direction for stocks, they’ve been busy “peeling back the layers” to dig up some bargains.
As for what they’ve spotted, he notes Apple AAPL, -0.16% has been “leading stocks out of the cellar,” while the VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF SMH, +0.45% also had a nice strong bust out of its recent market-driven funk, and Netflix NFLX, +2.53% had an in-your-face rebound. Of course, when the market went down last week, techs didn’t exactly escape.
MarketWatch This comes after investors yanked around $4 billion from the PowerShares QQQ Trust ETF last week, the most since the dot-com bubble burst, Guenthner notes, citing Bloomberg data.
“The herd clearly believes that the strongest stocks on the market will be the ones that have the farthest to fall if market weakness persists. But we’re not so sure about that … ,” said Guenthner.
Larry Tentarelli, of the Trend Trading Signals blog , attests further to tech strength. In emailed comments, he notes that Netflix didn’t even touch its key 50-day moving average last week when stocks were melting down.
Plus, the First Trust DJ Internet Index FDN, +0.33% didn’t close below its 50-day moving average, a “sign of extreme strength,” he says. Amazon AMZN, +0.67% Facebook FB, +1.20% , Netflix NFLX, +2.53% and PayPal PYPL, +0.04% are all top holdings for the First Trust ETF.
Key market gauges The Dow DJIA, -0.15% , S&P SPX, -0.06% and the Nasdaq COMP, +0.17% are in the red post data. Asian stocks had a mixed session , with the Nikkei NIK, -0.43% taking a strong-yen hit. European stocks SXXP, +0.37% got a shot in the arm from German growth data .
The dollar DXY, +0.19% is down again , mostly against the yen. Crude CLH8, -1.40% is dropping on worries data later will show rising supplies. Gold GCJ8, +0.37% took a hit after the data as well. The yield on the 10-year Treasury TMUBMUSD10Y, +1.60% has shot up to 2.875%.
See the Market Snapshot column for the latest action.
The economy January consumer price inflation shot up 0.5% , the biggest rise in five months, though that hasn’t shaken the overall picture too much. Core CPI rose 0.3%. Meanwhile, retail sales slumped in the same month , and a previous rise reported in December was wiped out.

The chart Watch maker Fossil FOSL, +75.33% shares are exploding, up 70% premarket after beating earnings expectations . The beleaguered company seems to have done the trick by announcing it will transition to wearable technology, which should boost margins.
This next chart shows just how Fossil has performed over the past two years, when it largely sat out the rally the rest of the market has enjoyed.
The buzz Netflix NFLX, +2.53% has lured in producer Ryan Murphy , the Hollywood bigwig behind such hits as “Glee” and “American Horror Story”, in a deal that could be worth as much as $300 million.
Chipotle CMG, +14.22% shares are up on news that Taco Bell CEO Brian Niccol will be the burrito chain’s new chief.
Hilton HLT, +1.05% , Dr Pepper DPS, -0.21% and Molson TAP, +2.64% are on the earnings list ahead of the bell, while Cisco CSCO, +0.69% is among the late-session highlights. Check out a Cisco preview here.
Dating app makers Tinder and Match are making moves to keep their female customers happy. Meanwhile, women would like Tinder men to stop venting so much.
“...like a rollercoaster going off the tracks.” Passengers describe moments of terror, moving into crash-position for landing when an engine cover blew off a United UAL, +0.27% flight over the Pacific Ocean. Luckily it landed fine in Hawaii , with no injuries.
The Quote: AFP/Getty Images Credit Suisse CEO Tidjane Thiam. “Yes, it has had a lot of attention, because this kind of short vol/long S&P trade was run by a lot of people at their own risk, and it worked well for a long time until it didn’t, which is generally what happens in markets.” — That was Credit Suisse CEO Tidjane Thiam, defending the bank’s short volatility product to CNBC as his company posted its third yearly loss in a row .
Its VelocityShares Daily Inverse VIX Short-Term Exchange-Traded Not XIV, +4.53% turned into a spectacular one-way bet last week, resulting in plans to shut it down, and some big pain for some investors .
Speaking of, someone has sent an anonymous letter to the SEC and CFTC claiming Wall Street’s “fear gauge” — the Cboe Volatility Index VIX, -14.26% — is being rigged .
